elections.notes: Conservative is the table's "Conservative (Total)" row: the Conservatives with the Scottish Unionists and the Ulster Unionists (10 seats), plus the National Liberals (16 seats, 985,343 votes). Labour includes the Labour Co-operative MPs; the Conservative seats include the Speaker. Seat changes are against the 1945 result; the table gives no separate gains and losses for Labour and the Conservatives because of the boundary changes. The party rows add up to 28,771,138 votes, 14 more than the table's total of 28,771,124, which is used for the Others share. Region winners are the party with most seats in each nation, from the infoboxes of the four "1950 United Kingdom general election in England/Scotland/Wales/Northern Ireland" articles (regionSource is the England one). England goes to the Conservatives with the National Liberals (253 seats to Labour's 251; the Conservatives alone had 243), following the national table's grouping. Northern Ireland's winner is the Ulster Unionist Party, which the national table counts with the Conservatives.

elections.notes: Conservative is the table's "Conservative (Total)" row: the Conservatives with the Scottish Unionists and the Ulster Unionists (9 seats), plus the National Liberals (19 seats, 1,058,138 votes). Labour includes the Labour Co-operative MPs; the Conservative seats include the Speaker. The infobox gives slightly different totals for Labour (13,948,385) and the Conservatives (13,717,851); the table's figures are used because they add up to its total of 28,596,594. The full results table gives Irish Labour 0 seats (with a gain and net +1) and an Independent Republican 1 seat; the summary table and the transfers-of-seats table give the seat (Belfast West) to Irish Labour and none to an Independent Republican, so that is used. Region winners are the party with most seats in each nation, from the infoboxes of the four "1951 United Kingdom general election in England/Scotland/Wales/Northern Ireland" articles (regionSource is the England one). Northern Ireland's winner is the Ulster Unionist Party, which the national table counts with the Conservatives. In Scotland in 1951 the Unionists with the National Liberals and Labour both won 35 seats; the Unionists had more votes (1,349,298 to 1,330,244), so Scotland is given to them.

elections.notes: Conservative is the table's "Conservative (Total)" row: the Conservatives with the Scottish Unionists and the Ulster Unionists (10 seats), plus the National Liberals (21 seats, 842,113 votes). Labour includes the Labour Co-operative MPs; the Conservative seats include the Speaker. The full results table repeats Labour's 1951 figures (295 seats, 13,948,883 votes) and the Liberals' 1951 vote (730,546); Labour 277 seats and 12,405,254 votes and Liberal 722,402 votes are taken from the infobox and the summary table, which agree with the table's own seat share (44.0%), vote shares, net change and totals. Sinn Féin's 2 seats come from the summary table (the full table shows 1 with a net change of +2); with these corrections the seats add up to 630 and the votes to the table's total of 26,759,729. Region winners are the party with most seats in each nation, from the infoboxes of the four "1955 United Kingdom general election in England/Scotland/Wales/Northern Ireland" articles (regionSource is the England one). Scotland goes to the Unionists with the National Liberals (36 seats to Labour's 34; the Unionists alone had 30), following the national table's grouping. Northern Ireland's winner is the Ulster Unionist Party, which the national table counts with the Conservatives.

elections.notes: SDP–Liberal Alliance is one row in the table; the summary table splits it into the Liberals (17 seats, 4,173,450 votes) and the Social Democrats (5 seats, 3,168,183 votes). The table lists parties with more than 500 votes; the total of 32,529,578 votes cast is given under it and used for the Others share. Labour includes the Labour Co-operative MPs; the Conservative seats include the Speaker. The summary table gives the SDLP 154,087 votes rather than 154,067. The Conservative share is 42.3% from the summary table (the full table says 42.2%, but 13,760,583 of 32,529,578 is 42.30%). It leaves out the smallest candidates; its rows add up to 27,135,415 of the 27,148,510 votes, which is used for the Others share. Labour includes the Labour Co-operative MPs. The Green Party of England and Wales (257,758 votes, 0.95%; the table rounds it to 1.0%) is under the 1% threshold and is in Others.
